source: pi-jev skill applicability wording (the requested activity is the candidate's activity; a shared topic alone is not enough), plus a choice question that shortlists a large catalog; v2: skillThreshold 0.6 → 0.5 so a 0.55 write-doc pick is not hidden when the catalog is trimmed; v3: scriptFirst — `paths:` globs on skills and routed rules match the paths a prompt names or a harness touched before Jev (a rule hit is selected, a skill hit is always asked); v4: injectThreshold 0.85 / injectMax 1 / injectMaxChars 12000 — the top skill at p ≥ 0.85 arrives with its SKILL.md body (selection is unchanged, so v3 metrics hold); v6: chooseDescriptionChars 260 → 160, a shorter stage-1 catalog (stage 2 keeps 420); v7: design intent 261023 (AGENTS.md) — no stage-1 single-choice shortlist: every candidate is asked as a bool in one call (directBelow 999), so a second needed skill is not squeezed out; general routing judgments (pasted payload is not the request, an error in a running app asks for reproduction) live in apply.instructions instead of skill descriptions; injectMax 1 → 2; v8: synthetic-scenario loop 261023 iteration 2 (docs/plan/261023-synthetic-routing-loop.md), train only — sibling candidates for another object were injected beside the needed one in several scenarios (analyze-claude-sessions beside analyze-pi-sessions; write-a-skill beside write-a-rule); iteration 1 also carried an 'object being edited' sentence that cost recall on app-error cases, dropped here

choose.noneDescription: No candidate's activity is requested: general questions, chit-chat, or work no listed skill or rule specialises in
choose.instructions: Which single candidate covers the main activity `request` asks for? Judge the work the user wants done, not the topics they mention: a shared topic alone is not enough. Read `conversation_excerpt` only when the request is a short follow-up that makes sense in context. Pick `none` when no candidate's activity is requested.

apply.instructions: Is the work `request` asks for the activity that this {kind} covers? {kind}: {name}. {description} Answer true only when the user is asking for that activity itself; a shared topic alone is not enough. Pasted material (inspector references, element JSON, logs, quoted text) is payload that says where, not what to do. An error reported in a running app asks for reproducing it there and fixing the code that throws. A candidate that serves a sibling object (another harness, tool, framework or product) is false unless the request names or implies that object. Read `conversation_excerpt` only when the request is a short follow-up.
apply.true: The requested activity is the one this {kind} covers
apply.false: The request only shares a topic with it, or asks for something else
